texts: mixed: the atoms themselves are right - Coraline Ash as doer, the lantern as the thing lit, the part-link to the Harbor Station, day 190, Year 1 and sundown - but 'lit' lemmatizes to the event class light while 'mist-light' two sentences later decomposes to the noun kind light, so one symbol ends up naming both an event class and a substance kind, and the two can unify. Write 'On day 190 of Year 1, Coraline Ash kindled the lantern of the Harbor Station at sundown.' - one word, and the collision is gone. Separate caveat you cannot write around: 'day 190 of Year 1' goes into the calendar day-of-month slot as (Day 190), because the translator has no day-of-year term.

good. the burning with the lantern as doer and mire-essence as what is consumed, plus the mire_essence to essence genus; the substance correctly stays a bare kind rather than gaining a spurious witness.

good. the produced mist-light gets its own witness, reused by the next two sentences, and mist_light is linked to its head noun light - that genus is the other half of the symbol collision noted on the first sentence, and fixing the verb there settles it.
good. 'at night' is carried as a time on the showing, and the mist-light is the symbol already in play rather than a second one.
good. 'a handful of nightmoths' becomes a moth group with the surface phrase recorded as its vague count (no number invented), and nightmoth is linked to moth.

mixed: the counting, Coraline Ash as counter, the lantern and 'the third watch' are all right, but the count of four is hung on the very group the previous sentence introduced as 'a handful' - which claims the handful numbered exactly four and that the four she counted were all of them, neither of which you said. The sentence itself is sound (our own rules already require a bare 'four nightmoths' to get its own group), so a re-parse fixes it; to state the link you probably intend and rule the merge out, write 'Coraline Ash counted four of the nightmoths at the lantern at the third watch.' - that makes the four a counted subset of the attracted moths and leaves the handful uncounted.
good. both the group landing and the per-member rule come out, and the rule is fireable, so a moth named later inherits its own landing.

good. the deposit keeps its roles, its place on the lantern and its per-member rule, and 'silken' is correctly exposed as a material adjective on the thread kind while the moths' group symbol is reused.

mixed: the collecting, the lantern as source, dawn and the date are right, but 'a small heap' is stamped onto the thread group the moths left, so the parse claims the heap she collected is exactly and entirely that deposit, and that the deposit is small. Again the sentence is sound and a compliant re-parse mints a separate heap; to take the trap away, write 'Coraline Ash collected a small heap of the silken threads from the lantern at dawn on day 191 of Year 1.' - 'of the' marks the heap as a portion of the threads on the lantern rather than the whole of them.
good. the carrying with the thread group as what is moved and Cauldron Hall as the goal, the hall both typed and named.
good. Hesper as the boiler, the threads as what is changed, sea-water as the place, the full date, and sea_water linked to water.

good. 'by evening' is kept as a deadline bound rather than a plain time - the right reading of 'by' - and the mire-essence that forms gets its own witness, distinct from the mire-essence the lantern burns.
good. the storing reuses that same mire-essence symbol, and the clay vessel is typed with its genus, with 'clay' correctly left inside the kind rather than predicated of the vessel.
good. 'the stored mire-essence' resolves to the symbol Hesper stored, so nothing is lost even though the participle gets no atom of its own, and sundown plus the date are carried.
